bias_targets.methodology: Swapping the order of candidate responses within evaluation prompts and measuring position consistency, conflict rates, and preference fairness.
Rephrasing original responses into more verbose versions without adding new information to see if the evaluator inappropriately favors longer texts.
Testing the tendency of LLM evaluators to favor responses containing specific details, authoritative citations, numerical values, or complex terminologies, even if factually incorrect.
Assessing whether an LLM acting as a judge assigns higher scores or preferences to responses that it generated itself compared to those generated by other models.
Evaluating if the judge model gives higher scores to responses that align with demographic stereotypes related to gender, race, and sexual orientation.
Testing whether LLM evaluators assign lower scores to or misinterpret expressions, contexts, or regional language variants originating from unfamiliar cultures.
Analyzing the evaluator's preference for visually appealing content (like emojis) or specific emotional tones (e.g., cheerful, sad, angry) regardless of the content's actual validity.
Checking if evaluators are inclined to give higher scores when explicitly provided with specific prestigious model names (e.g., labeling a response as 'gpt-4').
Observing whether the model unfairly penalizes responses written in non-standard English dialects or writing styles associated with marginalized groups.
Using the EVALBIASBENCH dataset to measure whether the evaluator is misled by artifacts such as empty references, content continuations, nested instructions, or familiar knowledge.
